title: Browse by theme
idea: Search picks one indicator. Browsing shows the choice.
summary: When you can't yet phrase the question, the Explore tab opens the whole catalogue as 12 thematic areas, and shows every version of an indicator.

chapters.label: When you only know the topic

transcript.text: Search is for when you know the question. This is for when you only know the topic.
The Explore tab opens the whole catalogue as twelve thematic areas, rather than a search box waiting for a question you cannot phrase yet.
Three filters narrow it: a location, a thematic area, and the UN body that published it. That last one is useful when you already trust a particular agency.
Open Health and the scale becomes obvious. Seven hundred and fifty-two indicators sit under this one heading.
So it breaks down again, into sub-themes with their own counts. Infectious diseases, mental health, reproductive and maternal health.

And here is the reason to browse rather than search. Adolescent birth rate appears four times, from W H O, UNICEF, the S D G database and U N D P. Browsing shows you the choice. Searching just picks one.
Use search when you know what you want. Use Explore when the real question is which indicator you should be using at all.
